gen-silkscreen-gf-jost: Spaghetti-thin letters with space around each one give Silkscreen a lo-fi, retro look before the text begins. Jost follows in sans-serif, clean and steady, its stroke one width throughout.
gen-silkscreen-gf-jura: Silkscreen lays out lo-fi, retro letters with room around each one, like spaghetti arranged along a line. Jura, in sans-serif, draws steady, bent-wire strokes and s curves that open wide.
gen-silkscreen-gf-k2d: Spaghetti-like lines and generous space around every letter give Silkscreen its lo-fi, retro look. But K2D holds a tube-like thickness through every bend, so longer paragraphs glide along smoothly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kodchasan: Silkscreen is lo-fi and retro, with space hovering around every letter. The sharpest quality here is the difference in character, since Kodchasan, in sans-serif, hangs its terminals open and skips calligraphic thinning.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kumbh-sans: Silkscreen looks lo-fi and retro, every letter set apart from its neighbours like spaghetti. But the real draw is contrast: Kumbh Sans keeps terminals cut short of the bowl, drawn with a fixed pen.
gen-silkscreen-gf-livvic: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen spaces every letter well apart from the next. What holds it together is Livvic, approachable and clean, with stress-free curves and a generously open c.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-1: Lo-fi through and through, Silkscreen leaves space around each letter, like spaghetti laid out. And the strongest pull is M PLUS 1, a sans with big open eyes on every e and a.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Letters with no pinched joints or flared ends, spaced like spaghetti, give Silkscreen its lo-fi, retro look. M PLUS Rounded 1c keeps paragraphs approachable, terminals stopping short of curling back.
gen-silkscreen-gf-manjari: Retro spaghetti lines spaced out letter by letter make Silkscreen feel properly lo-fi. Manjari then adds approachable curves with wide, unclosed terminals and a steady line weight.
gen-silkscreen-gf-murecho: Lo-fi curves that never thin out, with space around every letter, define Silkscreen. Murecho, in sans-serif, is modern and clean, its s curves opening generously at each end.
